name: Urea

lead: Urea is a natural component of skin moisturizing factor and is used in creams for dry, rough or scaling skin, including xerosis, eczema, keratosis pilaris and calloused heels. Low concentrations hydrate, while higher concentrations soften thick scale.
It has a long record in dermatology and good clinical support as a moisturizer and keratolytic.

paras: Urea attracts and binds water as a humectant and, at higher concentrations, breaks down hydrogen bonds in keratin to loosen and shed dead skin. It also appears to improve barrier function and antimicrobial peptide expression.
Mild stinging is the main side effect, especially on cracked or inflamed skin and at higher strengths. It is available without a prescription in most markets.
